article_title: Exploring students’ learning experience in online education: analysis and improvement proposals based on the case of a Spanish open learning university
citation: Rivera-Vargas, P., Anderson, T., & Alonso Cano, C. (2021). Exploring students’ learning experience in online education: analysis and improvement proposals based on the case of a Spanish open learning university. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-021-10045-0
title: UOC educational model integrating collaborative relationships, student autonomy, three-role human support, and digital resources
description: The article describes the UOC's educational model as "based on the integration of four fundamental elements": a horizontal collaborative student–teacher relationship, promotion of student autonomy and self-regulation, human support instantiated in consultant, tutor and technological support roles, and resources and content with active use of digital technologies. It is supported by evaluative flexibility through continuous evaluation tests and an environment favouring interactivity and cooperation.
requirements: Human support instantiated in consultant, tutor and technological support roles
Evaluative flexibility via continuous evaluation tests
key_sources: Rivera-Vargas, P., Anderson, T., & Alonso Cano, C. (2021). Exploring students’ learning experience in online education: analysis and improvement proposals based on the case of a Spanish open learning university. Education Tech Research Dev. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11423-021-10045-0

article_title: The Effectiveness of an Interactive Training Program in Developing a Set of Non-Cognitive Skills in Students at University of Petra
citation: Eman Gheith & Nahil M. Aljaberi. (2017). The Effectiveness of an Interactive Training Program in Developing a Set of Non-Cognitive Skills in Students at University of Petra. International Education Studies, 10(6). https://doi.org/10.5539/ies.v10n6p60
title: Interactive training program for six non-cognitive skills at University of Petra
description: A researcher-designed training program delivered through an obligatory "Teaching Thinking" faculty course, using "interactive training that largely depend on brainstorming, discussion, dialogue, team work, streaming of and illustrative movies." It targeted six non-cognitive skills: locus of control, planning, empathy, self-confidence, growth mindset, and grit. Students worked individually or in groups, concepts were introduced via short films and planned activities, there were no textbooks, and assessment used practical interactive projects rather than pen-and-paper exams.
requirements: Delivered through interactive activities performed individually or in groups, with concepts presented via short films or planned activities
constraints: The article reports the program did not significantly develop planning, locus of control, or self-confidence
target_learners: University of Petra undergraduates in the Faculty of Arts
examples: Group A attended the obligatory "Teaching Thinking" course with interactive tasks, no textbooks, and portfolio/project assessment instead of exams
key_sources: Eman Gheith & Nahil M. Aljaberi. (2017). The Effectiveness of an Interactive Training Program in Developing a Set of Non-Cognitive Skills in Students at University of Petra. International Education Studies, 10(6). https://doi.org/10.5539/ies.v10n6p60

article_title: Exploring peer tutoring experiences in improving nursing students' academic success and performance: A qualitative study among Emirati undergraduate nursing students.
citation: Dias Jacqueline Maria, Al Kaabi Fatema Salim Bati Salim, Al Hooti Sara Tamim, Hammadi Nada Osamah, Karim Rana, AlYateem Nabeel, Reefat Ahmed Fatma, Sara Abraham Mini, Seshan Vidya, Arsyad Sub Muhammad, Dias Ambrose Richard, Mottershead Richard (2025). Exploring peer tutoring experiences in improving nursing students’ academic success and performance: A qualitative study among Emirati undergraduate nursing students. F1000Research 14:1416. https://doi.org/10.12688/f1000research.172023.1
title: University of Sharjah peer tutoring program for undergraduate nursing students
description: A peer tutoring initiative within the Bachelor of Science in Nursing program at the University of Sharjah, studied between January and March 2025. The article states that "At the UOS, peer tutoring involves organized sessions where nursing students work together to review each other's work, provide constructive feedback, and support each other's academic growth." The program was evaluated through semi-structured interviews and open-ended surveys with tutors and tutees in a culturally and linguistically diverse student population.
requirements: Organized sessions with tutor and tutee roles; the article states creating a well-defined organizational structure for sessions is vital to promote purpose and confidence.
constraints: The study focused on nursing students at a single university, and its generalizability is limited per the authors.
target_learners: Undergraduate nursing students at the University of Sharjah
examples: The study included 17 undergraduate nursing students (6 tutors and 11 tutees) interviewed remotely via Microsoft Teams for 45 to 60 minutes; a pilot test with 5 tutors and 11 tutees refined the interview guides.
key_sources: Dias Jacqueline Maria, Al Kaabi Fatema Salim Bati Salim, Al Hooti Sara Tamim, Hammadi Nada Osamah, Karim Rana, AlYateem Nabeel, Reefat Ahmed Fatma, Sara Abraham Mini, Seshan Vidya, Arsyad Sub Muhammad, Dias Ambrose Richard, Mottershead Richard (2025). article_title: The application of blended teaching in medical practical course of clinical skills training.
citation: He Zhicheng, Li Hua, Lu Lan, Wang Qiang, Wu Qingming, Lu Lili. (2024). The application of blended teaching in medical practical course of clinical skills training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05730-6
title: UOOC online course 'Clinical Skills Training and Practice' with five clinical modules
description: The online component of the blended intervention was the UOOC course "Clinical Skills Training and Practice", divided into five clinical modules: internal medicine, surgery, gynecology, pediatrics, and emergency medicine. Each module contains "theoretical lecture videos, standardized operation demonstration videos, PPT resources, as well as supporting exercises and tests", plus a discussion board for teacher-student interaction. Online teaching constituted 25% of total class hours.
requirements: Access to the UOOC platform and electronic devices for students
Teacher presence on the discussion board to answer questions and post case material
constraints: Online teaching made up only 25% of class hours; the article states online teaching cannot fully substitute offline teaching for highly practical content
target_learners: undergraduate clinical medicine students in their fifth semester
target_learning_goals: clinical skills proficiency assessed by OSCE
examples: Students completed chapter tests and assignments on the platform after offline classes and could raise difficulties in the discussion area
key_sources: He Zhicheng, Li Hua, Lu Lan, Wang Qiang, Wu Qingming, Lu Lili. (2024). The application of blended teaching in medical practical course of clinical skills training. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-024-05730-6
